sections.title: Intermediate Concept
sections.content: Level 2 includes composite shapes and combinations. This involves adding two or more simple shapes to find total area, perimeter, or volume.

sections.title: Combined Area
sections.content: For a shape made of a rectangle and a semicircle: Total area = Rectangle area + Semicircle area. Semicircle area = 1/2 × π × r²

sections.title: Combined Perimeter
sections.content: Add all outer boundaries. Ignore inner dividing lines. Example: Rectangle + Semicircle perimeter = 2(l + w) + π × r

sections.title: Combined Volume
sections.content: For combined 3D shapes like cube + cylinder, total volume = cube volume + cylinder volume.

sections.title: Ratio and Similarity
sections.content:
For problems based on ratios, remember the relation:
Length ratio: a:b
Area ratio: a²:b²
Volume ratio: a³:b³

tricks.title: Composite Shape Area
tricks.explanation: Calculate areas of smaller parts separately and add. Use π ≈ 3.14 or 22/7.

tricks.title: Composite Perimeter
tricks.explanation: Add only outer boundaries; skip inner divisions.

tricks.title: Volume Combination
tricks.explanation: Calculate volume of each part separately and sum.

tricks.title: Ratio Based Calculation
tricks.explanation: Length ratio a:b → Area a²:b², Volume a³:b³.

tricks.title: Semicircle Area Fast
tricks.explanation: Half of circle area = 1/2 × π × r².

tricks.title: Cylinder Volume Quick
tricks.explanation: r² × h × π, do r² × h first for mental calculation.

tricks.title: Real-Life Application
tricks.explanation: Useful for flooring, tiling, and water tank calculations involving composite shapes.
tricks.example: Courtyard rectangle + semicircle → Total area ≈ 78.27 m²
